description: Approval digests computed by the reference executor (core/src/exec/machine.rs, core/src/exec/canonical.rs). Each vector is one approval request. STANDARD v1.1.0 section 5.14 states that a decision is valid only if the SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the shown values matches. What is shown when a step declares no `shows`, and the object added when a step asks again after a recheck, are the reference executor's behaviour; the Standard does not state them. This file is printable ASCII: any other character is written as a JSON \u escape, so no tool that normalises or transcodes text can change a vector.

fields.name: The vector's name, unique in this file.
fields.approval: The `approval` field of the step that asks, as the workflow declares it; null when the step has none.
fields.inputs: The step's resolved inputs. Present where the step declares no `shows`, so that `shown` is built from them.
fields.shown: The JSON array of shown values that the approval request carries.
fields.canonical: The RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization of `shown`. It is held here as a JSON string: the canonical text is the value a JSON parser returns for it.
fields.digest: The SHA-256 of the UTF-8 encoding of the canonical text, in lowercase hexadecimal: the digest the request carries and a decision repeats.

vectors.name: object
vectors.about: An object with a nested object. Members are written in the order of their names, whatever order the value had.

vectors.name: member_order
vectors.about: Member names sort by UTF-16 code unit: the empty name first, an uppercase letter before a lowercase one, a name before a longer name that begins with it. Array elements keep their order.

vectors.name: numbers
vectors.about: Numbers are written as ECMAScript writes the binary64 value, so -0.0, 1.0, 1e+21 and 1e-07 in the JSON text of `shown` become 0, 1, 1e+21 and 1e-7. 9007199254740992 is 2^53, the bound that section 5.14 gives for integers.

vectors.name: string_escapes
vectors.about: A string with a line feed, a tab, quotation marks, a backslash, U+0001, U+007F, U+00E9, U+20AC and U+1F600. The canonical text escapes the first five (U+0001 as `\u0001`, in lowercase) and holds the other four as themselves.

vectors.name: member_order_non_ascii
vectors.about: The member names of the sorting example in RFC 8785 section 3.2.3. U+1F600 is the surrogate pair D83D DE00 in UTF-16, so it sorts before U+FB33, although its code point is higher.

vectors.name: nesting
vectors.about: Objects and arrays nested, with true, false, null, an empty array and an empty object.

vectors.name: string_value
vectors.about: The shown value is a string.

vectors.name: array_value
vectors.about: The shown value is an array: it is one element of `shown`, not spliced into it.

vectors.name: number_value
vectors.about: The shown value is a number.

vectors.name: empty_list_value
vectors.about: The shown value is an empty array.

vectors.name: two_values_in_order
vectors.about: Two references: `shown` keeps the order of `shows`.

vectors.name: empty_shows
vectors.about: `shows` is an empty list: `shown` is the empty array.

vectors.name: no_shows
vectors.about: The `approval` field has no `shows`: the reference executor shows the step's resolved inputs, wrapped in an array.

vectors.name: no_approval_field
vectors.about: The step has no `approval` field and needs approval by the ontology: the reference executor shows the step's resolved inputs, wrapped in an array, as for `no_shows`.

vectors.name: asked_again_after_recheck
vectors.about: The recheck read a changed source, so the reference executor asks again (`on_change: reask`, the default). `shown` gains one object whose `recheck` member holds the value approved before (`previous`) and the value read now (`current`).
